model.name: Table of Contents
model.description:
Table of Content Widget

Widget for Figma to visualize pages as cards for index page, widget also includes statuses and descriptions for each page, very useful as a file guide for your team.


How to use:

  1. Add the widget to your Figma file.
  2. Use names without alphabetical letters to create separators between lists
  3. Use emojis at the beginning of the name of your pages to display them as an icon
  4. Click on the file description to change it.
  5. Click on status to change it to need.
  6. Enter a description for a page.


How does the icon work?

  • If the first symbols (up to 4) in the name of your file are emoji, the widget will display them separately as icons, 
  • If no emoji are used in the beginning then the widget will display the default blue icon (possible to turn it off in the property menu)


How to separate my pages?

  • If your page has no alphabetical letters (all languages are supported) then the widget will count it as a separator and will separate the cards


Property Menu:

  • Size: changing this property will configure the global scale of the widget, there are 4 sizes: extra small, small, medium, and large.
  • Theme: change the theme of the page cards, there are two options light and dark.
  • Show description: you can toggle on/off file descriptions, and descriptions for the page cards.
  • Show status: the toggle shows/hides the status in the page cards.
  • Show icon: the toggle shows icons separately or merged with the page and file name
  • Refresh: will refresh names, descriptions, and statuses, if you update it in the file or another copy of the widget in the same file.

model.name: SchemaFlow - SEO Content Model Builder
model.description:
The hardest part of building a content model is knowing where to start: What do I model? What do I call this content type? Using SchemaFlow, Schema.org schemas provide all of the answers, you just pick parts of the standard work best for you.

  1. Plan your websites and connect your content models to Google and other major search engines. 
  2. Use the Schema.org standard, which contains more than 750 content types, and model for almost any circumstance. 
  3. Use FigJam's easy visual interface to select the elements that your digital property needs.
  4. Use AI to kick-start your model building!

This free widget is brought to you by the Schematica team at schematica.io. If you need any help with your content model don’t hesitate to reach out to us. Happy Modeling!


Features

  1. Content Types: Select a source Schema.org schema to create a starting point for your content model.
  2. Content Elements: Select Schema.org schema properties based on the selected schema to add detail to your content model.
  3. Generate with AI: Use an AI API like OpenAI to generate a content model for you! Just tell the AI what you are trying to build and add its suggestions to FigJam.
  4. Example content: Select the expected format of your content to add example content for each schema property and increase content model understanding.
  5. Export: Select all or part of the model to export in the JSON-LD format, Contentful JSON format, or a Kontent.ai file. With example content included, the JSON-LD export is ready to use on your webpages as markup for search indexing. Easily import new content types into your Contentful space Kontent.ai project and add your own customizations.


How to use SchemaFlow

  1. Run the widget to add a schema to the FigJam Canvas
  2. Click the ‘Add Properties’ button
  3. Select a schema type and browse that type’s properties
  4. Choose the properties you want and click ‘Add Properties’
  5. Select an ‘Expected Type’ for a property to add example content to your model
  6. Clicking ‘Export JSON-LD’ will create a JSON-LD file for the selected schema


What is a Schema?

A schema is an outline or model that defines how information should be created or organized. Many systems, such as databases, content management systems (CMSs), and others, use schemas to define the rules for the information that they store. Templates and content models are types of schemas that can define required sections, required metadata, maximum length, and other rules for a specific type of content. 


What is Schema.org?

Schema.org is best known for maintaining the standard schema that Google and other search engines use to ‘understand’ content on the web. Millions of webpages use markup based on schema.org schemas to enhance how their search results are ranked and displayed by Google and other search engines.


Why use Schema.org for content modeling?

In addition to providing a great foundation for content modeling, Schema.org schemas provide significant benefits when content gets used on the web. It is a breeze for developers to create the schema.org markup required by search engines when the content structure already maps perfectly to schema.org. Or, even easier, just export the necessary markup directly from FigJam with SchemaFlow.

Have a question, idea, or just need help with content modeling? We would love to talk to you! Send us a message at tech@schematica.io

  • 5-6 players: Start with 15 tiles each
